scheme_name: "Subsidy for Orthodox & Speciality Tea Unit for Plant & Machinery" under the "Assam Tea Industries Special Incentives Scheme"
description:
The "Subsidy for Orthodox & Speciality Tea Unit for Plant & Machinery" is a significant component of the Assam Tea Industries Special Incentives Scheme. 

This scheme was launched by the Government of Assam in 2017. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to promote the production of orthodox and specialty tea in Assam. 

Assam is known for its rich tea heritage and is one of the largest tea-producing states in India. 

The government aims to enhance the quality and value of tea produced in the region. 

The scheme intends to provide financial assistance to tea producers for setting up or upgrading their production units. 

The target is to increase the production of orthodox and specialty tea by at least 20 percent over the next five years. 

This initiative is expected to create employment opportunities in the tea sector. 

The scheme also aims to improve the income levels of tea growers and workers in Assam. 

The financial assistance provided under this scheme is specifically for the purchase of plant and machinery. 

Eligible units can receive a subsidy of up to 30 percent of the total cost of plant and machinery. 

The maximum subsidy amount is capped at ₹50 lakh per unit. 

This means that if a tea producer invests ₹1 crore in plant and machinery, they can receive a subsidy of ₹30 lakh. 

The subsidy is aimed at both new units and existing units that are upgrading their machinery. 

To be eligible for this subsidy, the tea unit must be registered with the Tea Board of India. 

The unit must also be located in Assam. 

There are no specific age limits for the applicants. 

However, the applicant must be a legal entity such as an individual, partnership firm, or company. 

The income criteria for eligibility are not strictly defined. 

However, preference is given to small and medium enterprises in the tea sector. 

The application process involves several steps. 

First, the applicant must fill out the application form available on the Assam Government's official website. 

The application form requires details about the unit, including its registration number, location, and the type of tea produced. 

Next, the applicant must submit a detailed project report. 

This report should outline the proposed investment in plant and machinery. 

It should also include the expected outcomes in terms of production capacity and employment generation. 

The applicant must provide copies of relevant documents. 

These documents include the registration certificate, tax identification number, and bank account details. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the Assam Tea Board. 

The board will assess the project report and the viability of the proposed investment. 

If approved, the subsidy will be disbursed in a phased manner. 

The first installment of the subsidy is typically released after the purchase of the machinery is completed. 

The remaining amount may be disbursed based on the production targets achieved. 

The Assam Tea Board is the implementing authority for this scheme. 

The board operates under the Department of Tea and is responsible for promoting tea cultivation and processing in Assam. 

For further assistance, applicants can contact the Assam Tea Board at their official office in Guwahati. 

The contact number for the Assam Tea Board is +91-361-273-1900. 

The email address for inquiries is at tea.assam@gmail.com. 

The scheme is part of a broader initiative to revitalize the tea industry in Assam. 

The state government has recognized the potential of orthodox and specialty teas in accessing international markets. 

These types of teas are often sold at higher prices compared to regular black tea. 

The global demand for specialty teas is increasing, and Assam aims to capitalize on this trend. 

The Assam Tea Industries Special Incentives Scheme also includes other benefits for tea producers. 

These benefits include training programs for tea growers on best practices in tea cultivation and processing. 

The government is also working on improving infrastructure facilities in tea-growing areas. 

This includes better transportation and storage facilities to enhance the supply chain. 

The scheme has been positively received by the tea industry stakeholders. 

Many tea producers have reported increased interest in producing orthodox and specialty teas. 

The government has also conducted awareness programs to inform producers about the scheme. 

These programs aim to educate tea growers on the benefits of upgrading their production units. 

The Assam Tea Board has been actively promoting the scheme through various channels. 

The board has organized workshops and seminars to engage with tea producers. 

The subsidy for plant and machinery is expected to significantly boost the competitiveness of Assam's tea industry. 

This initiative aligns with the government's vision of making Assam a global hub for specialty teas. 

The scheme is expected to contribute to the overall economic development of the state. 

The tea industry is a major source of employment in Assam. 

It provides livelihoods to millions of people in the region. 

By enhancing the quality of tea production, the scheme aims to increase the income levels of these workers. 

The government has set a timeline for the implementation of this scheme. 

The subsidy program is expected to run for five years from its launch in 2017. 

Regular evaluations will be conducted to assess the impact of the scheme on the tea industry. 

The Assam government is committed to supporting the tea sector through various initiatives. 

This includes financial assistance, training, and infrastructure development. 

The subsidy for orthodox and specialty tea units is a crucial step in this direction. 

Overall, the scheme represents a strategic effort to enhance the quality and marketability of Assam's tea. 

It aims to ensure that Assam remains a key player in the global tea market. 

The focus on specialty teas is particularly important given the changing consumer preferences. 

As consumers increasingly seek high-quality and unique tea products, Assam is well-positioned to meet this demand. 

The subsidy for plant and machinery is a vital tool in achieving these objectives. 

This initiative not only supports tea producers but also contributes to the sustainable development of the region. 

In conclusion, the "Subsidy for Orthodox & Speciality Tea Unit for Plant & Machinery" under the Assam Tea Industries Special Incentives Scheme is a comprehensive program designed to uplift the tea industry in Assam. 

It provides substantial financial support and aims to foster innovation and quality in tea production.
